author: Evan Denton
title: Iowa female coaches, players reflect on National Girls and Women in Sports Day - NewsBreak
text:
By Evan Denton ,
1 hours ago
Feb. 4 is National Girls and Women in Sports Day. It’s meant to be a chance to honor the achievements of women athletes, coaches and leaders.
The University of Iowa has a long history of helping advance women’s sports. Current Iowa female athletes and coaches said it’s great to use their platforms to show how far women’s sports have come, and how they can continue to grow.
“I just make sure in all my actions, like, I work hard, I support my teammates, I cheer everybody on,” said Journey Houston, an Iowa freshman guard. “I just want to be somebody that young girls look up to. I still look up to older women, but I kind of am a role model now.”
“The high school girls athletic association, you know, their tag line is ‘Iowa girl,’ and so when you grow up in Iowa you kind of just thought it was like that where people cared about sports, and they are excited about it, they supported it,” said Jan Jensen, Iowa women’s basketball’s head coach. “Then as you grew up, and as you go to college, and you coach in college, you realize that it’s really not like that. Even more reason why my pride is great in the state, but certainly the University of Iowa with the great leadership of Dr. Christine Grant.”
“It’s an honor and a privilege to be at a university that has had so much history of women and people fighting for the growth of women’s sports and just opportunity for women,” said Jennifer Llewellyn, Iowa women’s gymnastics’ head coach. “It’s really exciting to be at a university that has a female president, and a female athletic director, and I think it’s very inspiring for our athletes to see women in charge, too, because it shows them what is possible, and almost gives them more freedom to be who they are.”
